description:
FILED s509+ (Fable, 2026-10-06) from probing the cases in https://perlmonks.org/index.pl?node_id=44722 ("On Parsing Perl") for a reddit answer.  Probed vs perl 5.40.3 at main ad1ede72.

PPI decides `/` after a bareword is DIVISION, then ends the statement at the next `;` and starts a comment at the next `#` -- so the closing `/` of the match is in ANOTHER statement or inside a Comment token, where `_repair_word_match` (#351, #872, #484) does not look.

  $_ = "x 25 ; # y";
  sin  / 25 ; # / ; die "regex";     perl: dies (sin(/ 25 ; # /))   PCL: no die -- sin()/25, SILENT WRONG
  my @r = (sin /;/, 9);               perl: 0.84.. 9                   PCL: statement DROPPED (loud; dies there)
  sub one {...}  my $v = one /a;b # x/;  perl: one(1)                   PCL: "Illegal division by zero" (one() / a)

PPI dump of line 1: Statement[Word sin, Operator /, Number 25, Structure ;] + Comment `# / ; die "x";`.

RIGHT TODAY (same probe session, all identical to perl): `time / 25 ; # / ; die` (division), `split /,/`, `sin /foo/`, `FOO / 7` (use constant), `no_args / 25` (declared ()), an IMPORTED () sub `aaa / 25`, `one_arg /foo/`, `normal /o,b/, 2`, imported `bbb /foo/`, `BEGIN { *zzz = sub () { 42 } } zzz / 2`.

SIZE: the shape is rare outside deliberately adversarial code (a match with a `;` or ` #` in it, written without parens after a word that takes arguments).  Not scheduled.  The cheap discriminating measurement before any fix: count the shape over the four populations -- a repair candidate is a Statement ending `WORD-that-is-not-a-term / ... ;` whose following siblings (to end of LINE, comment included) hold an unescaped `/`.  A fix belongs with the other token repairs (re-lex the line from the `/`), and it gets a ppi-upstream-bugs.md section only if PPI could know better -- for a BUILTIN that takes an argument (sin) it could; for a user sub it cannot.

SIBLING, noted in #2610: `BEGIN { eval q{sub zzz () { 42 }} } print zzz / 2` -> perl 21, PCL 0 (the name is unknown when the file is parsed, so it reads as the string "zzz").

ADDED same day (the reddit thread, r/perl 1wz2p7a -- the asker is merlyn himself; the other operator-or-term characters probed after a constant vs after an arg-taking sub: `% & * < << - + . {` and `x` ALL identical to perl).  One more member, LOUD: an EMPTY pattern after an arg-taking user sub -- `sub args {...}  print "x ", (args //, 2)` -> perl `x args(1 2)`, PCL drops the statement ("Handle single node of unknown type"; PPI lexes `//` as defined-or).  `split //, $s`, a bare `//` in a condition and `$u // 4` are right.

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 64353611) ===
VERDICT: LIVE -- the three rows as filed: `sin / 25 ; # / ; die "regex"` inside an eval -> perl died=yes, PCL died=no (silent) ;
  `my @r = (sin /;/, 9)` and `my $v = one /a;b # x/` -> one LOUD drop of the rest of the line ("Bug. Fell through. Missing case").
LABEL: silent (the first row; subject now says so).

=== s543d (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21; the repair-pass audit, docs/ppi-fix-at-source-s527.md §10) ===
SPLIT BY WHO CAN KNOW.  The BUILTIN row (`sin / 25 ; # / ; die`) is PPI's to fix: on PCL's branch `sin /;/`, `print /x/`, `when /x/`, `1 while /x/g` are still DIVISION, because Token/Whitespace.pm's `/` arm asks its `%MATCHWORD` table (return split if unless grep map ...) and not `_term_expected` (toke.c yyl_slash: under XTERM `/` starts scan_pat) -- proposed as member 1 of PPI batch 11; once PPI reads the whole match, the `;` and `#` inside it are pattern text and this row is fixed at the source.  The USER-SUB rows (`one /a;b # x/`, `args //, 2`) are the word-is-a-term family (only the prototype table knows `one` takes arguments): PCL's, `_repair_word_match`'s re-lex would have to reach across the `;` / the Comment -- not a branch item.  Re-probed on the s543d tree: `one /a;b # x/` and `args //, 2` still DIFF (perl `one(1)`, `x args(1 2)`).
_repair_word_match's fires on the 2,053-file list: 4 files / 12 fires, after `when` (t/op/switch.t x2), `while` (t/re/pat_advanced.t), `ok` (t/re/pat.t x7, pat_advanced.t, pat_re_eval.t).

=== DONE (s543f) -- the BUILTIN row; the residue is the user-sub half ===
PCL's PPI group BE (docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md §71, branch pcl-s543f d27d0c37): a `/` after a builtin that takes an operand is a match on the branch -- Token/Whitespace.pm's `/` arm asks `_term_expected` in place of its word list -- so `sin / 25 ; # / ; die "regex"` reads the whole pattern and the die RUNS (perl died=yes; main died=no, the silent wrong of this task's first row), and `my @r = (sin /;/, 9)` lowers (it died "term walker declined a Regexp::Match operand" in PExpr once the token was right: `_term_extent` now takes a Regexp token as a primary).  Probe table scratch/s543f/p1 (42 rows, perl -> main -> tree), rows s07 s08: base DIFF, tree SAME.  Guard: Pl/t/ppi-token-rows-01.t "§71: sin / 25 ; # / ; die runs the die; ..." (fails on main), registry row §71, twins §71.
RESIDUE (still LIVE, the user-sub half -- only a declaration says the word takes a list, PCL's _repair_word_match / the prototype table, §11): `sub one {...} my $v = one /a;b # x/;` (perl one(1); main and tree "Illegal division by zero") and `sub args {...} print "x ", (args //, 2)` (perl `x args(1 2)`; main and tree drop).  Subject rewritten to the residue.

SUBJECT corrected (s543f): the residue is LOUD -- `one /a;b # x/` dies "Illegal division by zero", `args //, 2` drops the statement; the silent row was the builtin one, fixed.


=== s543i (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-22; PPI batch 12 member 4) -- the residue re-measured: REACHABLE only by a repair that crosses a statement end, so it stays LOUD by design ===
Both rows still LOUD on base 8aaf1a29 and on the s543i tree: `sub one {...} my $v = one /a;b # x/;` dies "Illegal division by zero" (perl one(1)), `sub args {...} print "x ", (args //, 2)` drops (perl `x args(1 2)`); and one more member of the same derail, found with #5231's fix: `print STDOUT /;/` (a `;` inside the pattern after a handle) drops on both.  Why they stay: PPI ends the statement at the `;` (or starts a Comment at the `#`, or lexes `//` as the defined-or) BEFORE the pattern's closing `/`, and only a declaration -- `one` / `args` take a list, `STDOUT` is a handle -- says the `/` opened a match; `_repair_word_match`'s close scan stops at a statement-level `;` on purpose (task #872: a scan past it repaired the wrong `/`).  A repair would have to re-lex across statements and comments from the `/` (a new repair shape: the standing rule says no).  TRIAGE: LOUD, rare (a `;` / ` #` inside a match written without parens after a word that takes a list), never silent -- OUT of the next batches unless a real program needs it.
frequency_reason: a regex after a paren-less user-sub call whose body holds `;` or `#` (first pass from the subject, the reviewing session 2026-11-24)
subject: LOUD residue (the user-sub half of PPI section 11): a regex after a USER sub whose body holds ; or # -- one /a;b # x/ dies Illegal division by zero (perl one(1)), args //, 2 drops; the builtin row (sin / 25 ; # / ; die, the silent one) is fixed at the source, s543f group BE (section 71)
triage_reason: a regex after a word, cut by PPI at `;` / `#` (the PPI branch)
